model_output.verdict: A marketing executive whose leadership remit and commercial results are easy to follow.
write_up: This is a strong executive marketing resume! Your progression from Senior Marketing Manager to Chief Marketing Officer comes with team sizes, budgets, and results across demand generation, product launches, and brand work. A recruiter can see both what you led and what changed.

The account-based marketing line at Viridian is a good model: it names the program you built, its pipeline contribution, and the change in win rates. Your current role also puts the 45-person organization and $25M budget right up front.

Let's add what changed in the Novara launch process, then leave the rest of the story to do its work. Your resume is unlikely to be the reason you don't get a callback; the competitiveness of the role and a referral can also matter.

cards.line: - I decided to revamp the product launch process, shortening time-to-market by 30% and increasing launch success rate to 90%, resulting in a $15M incremental revenue increase over 2 years.
cards.cannot_tell: The launch results are substantial, but a recruiter can't tell what you changed in the process. That decision is worth showing alongside the results.
cards.example: I decided to revamp the product launch process by [process change], shortening time-to-market by 30% and increasing launch success rate to 90%, resulting in a $15M incremental revenue increase over 2 years.
cards.question: What did you change in the product launch process?

cards.line: - I built and executed a comprehensive account-based marketing (ABM) program that increased pipeline contribution by $50M annually, lifting win rates by 15% among Fortune 500 clients.
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this one. It gives the reader a named program, your ownership, and the clients it reached, all in one line.
